page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3s.4xlarge is a big data and storage-dense instance type engineered for high-capacity data processing and retention. Hosted on a KVM hypervisor, the instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8369B processors clocked at 2.7 GHz across an x86_64 architecture. The system configuration provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core.

A primary architectural feature of the ecs.d3s.4xlarge is its massive bundled local storage array, providing 95,348 GB of local hard disk drive (HDD) capacity directly attached to the host. Network connectivity is supported by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth interface. The instance does not include integrated graphical accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its operational profile entirely toward bulk data workloads rather than acceleration-dependent or edge-facing tasks.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of this instance is shaped by its dense local HDD storage. Delivering tens of terabytes on magnetic media allows organizations to optimize cost per gigabyte stored for high-volume data streams compared to high-performance solid-state tiers. The primary tradeoff lies in storage I/O performance: magnetic media delivers sequential throughput suitable for stream logging and distributed file blocks, but exhibits high latency and low IOPS under random access patterns.

The ecs.d3s.4xlarge is structured for distributed big data processing, data warehousing nodes, Apache Hadoop clusters, Apache Kafka log partitions, large-scale sequential data analytics, and cold to warm archival databases where massive density takes precedence over ultra-low latency storage access.
